analysis: The closest option now studies art history, archaeology, museums and art historiography alongside film and rhetoric. West African heritage, empire and histories of gender and race provide concrete comparative cases. Documentary, historical research and creative writing develop different ways of constructing and communicating cultural accounts. Sociology and politics provide tools for analysing authority and representation. Marketing, market research and general leadership courses were removed because they contributed less to this arts and cultural studies target.

The environmental option combines climate science, resource lifecycles, water adaptation and applied partner research with environmental justice, governance, legal institutions and cultural representation. Media and the Environment and Communicating the Climate Crisis establish its humanities strand. Indigenous histories and sociology support study of unequal effects and community responses. The move from geochemistry, geology and resource engineering to media, sustainability and Indigenous history improves the response to the official cultural and political emphasis. Research in a Sustainable Delta takes its planned first-term slot.

The digital option uses Python, data science, algorithms, databases and neural networks to understand the mechanisms behind automated media and decisions. AI Ethics gives explicit attention to bias and accountability, while film history, media archaeology, television, race, visual art and documentary make culture the application domain. Public Policy Analysis provides a regulatory analysis method. Qualitative methods and civil society support investigation of how communities respond to digital change. This is a cultural and technical response without claiming a dedicated creative AI studio.

The three options differ by 127.5, 90 and 150 EC each way. Cultural justice is already represented in the closest option through histories of gender and empire, race and media, social theory and political institutions. The environmental and digital options add different methods and advanced content. All three are feasible and reach the limit. The alignment leaves meaningful gaps where UCR lacks a specialist unit.
constructionStop: Three academically viable and distinct compositions meet the maximum.

alignment.rationale: Both analyse persuasion, argument and rhetorical traditions and develop communication skills.
Both teach close observation and interpretation of artworks. UCR places those skills within Western art history.
Both interpret objects in social context. UCR works with archaeological material, while UvA draws on art history and museum collections.
Both examine how art and institutions shape cultural authority. UCR focuses on modern art and museums.
Both reconsider established accounts of the past and the methods that produce them. UCR examines the writing of art history.
Both study how the form and circulation of media affect knowledge. UCR ranges across media technologies, while UvA focuses on historical written and printed material.
Both consider cultural and ethical responses to ecological change. UCR focuses on environmental representation in media.
Both examine how cultural representation can reinforce exclusion or challenge it. UCR focuses on race and media.
UvA gives dedicated practice in writing about culture and politics across formats.
UvA brings philosophical inquiry into direct dialogue with art and culture.
UCR rhetoric is aligned to the introductory UvA course. The second UvA course develops formal analysis and evaluation of arguments.
UvA studies maps as cultural evidence and practises historical cartographic analysis.
UvA studies theatre and the institutions and societies it helps shape.
Both use gender to rethink historical narratives. UCR examines a wider range of histories of gender and identity.
Both study historical connections across regions. UCR concentrates on empires and their legacies.
Both use political theory to examine power across borders. UvA also considers global challenges through cultural and political examples.
Both introduce social theory and cultural context. UvA gives sustained attention to feminist, queer and decolonial critiques.
